# Welcome — test the Network Topology Exporter against your lab

You're a Grafana employee who wants to run the exporter against your own lab network and see the data show up here. **Six steps, about 10 minutes.**

**What you'll deploy:**
- The exporter (Docker container) on a host that can reach your lab via SNMP
- Grafana Alloy alongside it, shipping `tester_id`-labeled metrics + logs to *this* stack
- A unique `tester_id` so every dashboard in this folder can filter to your data

**Prereqs:** Docker + Docker Compose v2 on a Linux/macOS host with SNMP reachability to at least one LLDP- or CDP-speaking device.

---

## 1 — Pick a unique `tester_id`

Short, lowercase, kebab-case. Examples: `alice-homelab`, `bob-aws-vpc`, `colinwood-clos`.

This becomes a Prometheus label across every metric and log line you ship. Pick it once and keep it stable — changing it later splits your data into two unrelated series.

## 2 — Get a Grafana Cloud token for *this* stack

You're an admin on `networko11ydev.grafana.net`, so you can self-issue a write token.

**Easiest path** — from inside the stack itself:

1. Open <https://networko11ydev.grafana.net/connections/add-new-connection>
2. Search for **"Hosted Prometheus metrics"** → click → **"View details"**
3. Under **API token**, click **"Generate now"**. Name it `tester-<your-id>`.
4. Copy the token (starts with `glc_eyJ…`). **Save it — you cannot see it again.**
5. Repeat for **"Hosted Loki logs"** if you want a separate logs token, or reuse the same access policy if you scope it `logs:write` as well.

**Alternative** — one token for metrics + logs + traces via Access Policies:

1. Click your avatar (top right) → **"Manage account"** to open the grafana.com admin.
2. Left nav → **Security** → **Access policies** → **Create access policy**
3. Scopes: `metrics:write`, `logs:write`, `traces:write`. Realms: this stack.
4. On the policy, **Add token**, copy the value.

You only need ONE token; the same value works for both `prometheus.remote_write` and `loki.write` in the Alloy config.

## 3 — Get the code & build the image

```bash
git clone https://github.com/colinedwardwood/network-topology-exporter.git
cd network-topology-exporter
docker build -t network-topology-exporter:latest .
```

## 4 — Configure the harness

```bash
cd deploy/test-harness
cp config.yaml.example       config.yaml
cp alloy/config.alloy.example alloy/config.alloy
```

**Edit `config.yaml`** — change exactly one block:

```yaml
discovery:
  scope:
    cidr_allow_list:
      - "10.0.0.0/24"   # <-- YOUR lab's CIDR (the subnet your devices live on)
```

**Edit `alloy/config.alloy`** — only two placeholders to fill in. Everything else (URLs, user IDs) is pre-filled for this stack.

| Placeholder | Replace with |
|---|---|
| `YOUR_GLC_TOKEN` (appears twice) | your `glc_eyJ…` token from Step 2 |
| `YOUR_TESTER_ID` (appears twice) | your tester_id from Step 1 |

```bash
# Quick one-liners:
sed -i "" "s/YOUR_GLC_TOKEN/glc_eyJ.../g"  alloy/config.alloy   # macOS
sed -i "s/YOUR_GLC_TOKEN/glc_eyJ.../g"     alloy/config.alloy   # Linux
sed -i "" "s/YOUR_TESTER_ID/alice-homelab/g" alloy/config.alloy # macOS
```

> If you want to ship OTLP traces, the Tempo username is `1497055` and the push endpoint is `tempo-prod-30-prod-us-east-3.grafana.net:443`. The default harness doesn't ship traces yet — only add if you've enabled OTLP push in the exporter config.

## 5 — Start the stack

```bash
export SNMP_COMMUNITY=public          # or whatever your lab community is
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f topology-exporter | grep cycle
```

Look for `discovery cycle complete` within the first minute.

## 6 — Verify

Wait 60 seconds, then **refresh this page** and pick your `tester_id` from the dropdown at the top. The big status panel above should switch from **RED** to **GREEN**.

Then visit (all auto-filter to your tester_id once selected here):

- **[01. Test Harness Health](/d/harness-health)** — cycle duration, failure reasons, conflict counts
- **[02. Topology Data](/d/topology-data)** — devices and edges as tables
- **[03. Topology Graph](/d/topology-graph)** — interactive node graph
- **[04. Topology Schedule](/d/topology-schedule)** — when discovery last ran

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | First thing to check |
|---|---|
| Status panel stays RED after 2 min | `docker logs test-harness-alloy-1` — almost always a token typo, missing `:443`, or wrong remote_write URL |
| Exporter found 0 devices | `docker exec test-harness-topology-exporter-1 nc -zvu -w 2 <device-ip> 161` — UDP/161 must succeed |
| Devices found but 0 edges | Devices need LLDP or CDP enabled. Verify SNMP can read `lldpRemTable`: `snmpwalk -v2c -c <community> <device-ip> 1.0.8802.1.1.2.1.4` |
| `permission denied` on `/var/run/docker.sock` | Add your user to the `docker` group, or prefix `docker compose` with `sudo` |
| LLDP edges appear but they look like MAC addresses, not interface names | Expected when the device advertises `lldpRemPortIdSubtype=3` (MAC). The exporter shows the MAC; this is faithful to the wire. |

## Tear-down

```bash
cd deploy/test-harness
docker compose down -v        # -v removes the snapshot volume
```

---

**Questions / bugs:** open an issue at <https://github.com/colinedwardwood/network-topology-exporter/issues>, or ping `#network-o11y` in Slack.
